defs_parts: Eight labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Video only: the term comes from a video lecture, and is not in the course text or on the term list.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A particle is one short-lived point, and the emitter is what spawns it.
Amount caps how many are alive, and the rate is amount divided by lifetime.
Explosiveness one makes a burst, and one shot stops after a single cycle.
Gravity adds speed downward, and damping takes speed away.
A GPU node keeps its movement rules in its ParticleProcessMaterial.
Restraint keeps most effects quiet, so the important one reads clearly.
bookends.command: Quiz me on particle effect terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms amount, emission rate, lifetime, explosiveness, one shot, preprocess, spread, initial velocity, gravity and damping. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game effect, and the answer waits for your reply.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
